prompt:
Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

TEXT_G:
Stronger Economy, Fairer Society: Opportunity for Everyone

The Liberal Democrats set out a five‑year plan for an open, optimistic, outward‑looking UK that combines sound finances with social justice, green growth and equal rights.

Responsible finances and fair taxes
- Balance the structural current budget by 2017/18 with a fair mix of savings and taxes on wealth, big banks and polluters; debt to fall year on year thereafter.
- No rises in headline Income Tax, NI, VAT or Corporation Tax; raise the Personal Allowance to at least £12,500; clamp down on avoidance and non‑dom status; levy on high‑value property.

Prosperity for all: a high‑skill, low‑carbon economy
- Long‑term Industrial Strategy; double economy‑wide R&D; expand apprenticeships and National Colleges; devolve economic levers locally.
- Reform finance: stronger British Business Bank; more competition, community and alternative finance.
- Green leadership: Zero Carbon Britain by 2050; expand the Green Investment Bank; end unabated coal by 2025; set a 2030 power decarbonisation target with up to 60% renewables; back community energy; tight fracking rules with revenues funding the transition.
- Modern infrastructure: HS2 as part of a UK‑wide network, rail electrification, city‑region transport, clean air zones, ultra‑low‑emission vehicle rollout, near‑universal high‑speed broadband.
- Open, trading nation: stay in a reformed EU, complete the Single Market, support fair trade deals, welcome talent and students.

Real help for families and work
- Expand free childcare to 20 hours for ages 2–4 and from nine months for working parents, complete Tax‑Free Childcare.
- Make work pay through Universal Credit; protect disability benefits; promote flexible work and Shared Parental Leave; transparency to close the gender pay gap; Living Wage in central government.
- Pensions: make the Triple Lock permanent; continue auto‑enrolment; fairer, simpler savings.

World‑class education, cradle to college
- Protect funding from nursery to 19; strengthen the Pupil Premium; qualified teachers in every class.
- End child illiteracy and innumeracy by 2025; a slim core curriculum including PSHE, financial literacy and age‑appropriate SRE; independent standards body.
- Double firms hiring apprentices; improve FE; widen university access and protect income‑contingent finance; discount bus travel for 16–21s.

Health, care and wellbeing
- Invest at least £8bn extra a year in England’s NHS by 2020; integrate health and social care; improve GP access.
- Parity for mental health with waiting‑time standards and a £500m uplift; better children’s and perinatal services; crisis care that ends use of police cells.
- Support carers with a £250 annual bonus and new rights; cap care costs; raise care quality.
- Public health first: curb junk food marketing to children, tobacco levy, proportionate e‑cig rules, minimum alcohol pricing, cleaner air and warmer homes.

Homes and greener places
- Build 300,000 homes a year with Garden Cities, public‑land development and a Housing Investment Bank.
- Boost affordable housing; “Rent to Own” and Help to Rent; stronger tenant protections.
- Green Buildings Act: upgrade homes to EPC Band C (fuel‑poor by 2027); council tax discount for major efficiency improvements.
- Five Green Laws: Nature, Zero Carbon, Green Transport, Resource Efficiency/Zero Waste, and Green Buildings; expand accessible green space and protect wildlife; support sustainable farming and fair food chains.

Freedom, justice and secure communities
- Protect the Human Rights Act; pass a Digital Bill of Rights; a second Freedoms Act; evidence‑led policing with local Police Boards; a Victims’ Bill of Rights.
- Tackle violence against women and girls; rehabilitate offenders with smart non‑custodial sentences; health‑led drug policy.
- Restore full entry/exit checks; fair, efficient asylum; welcome skilled migrants and students.

Power to people and nations
- Home Rule within a federal UK; a Constitutional Convention; votes at 16; proportional representation (STV) for Commons and local government; reformed Lords; cap big money in politics; devolution on demand in England.

Britain in the world
- Lead in the EU, NATO, UN and Commonwealth; support a safe, reformed EU; climate leadership (EU −50% by 2030; zero‑carbon UK by 2050); step down nuclear posture while maintaining security; keep aid at 0.7%; champion human rights and LGBT+ equality worldwide.

TEXT_F:
Labour’s 2015 manifesto sets out a plan to make Britain work for working people, anchored by a Budget Responsibility Lock: every promise is fully funded with no new borrowing; the deficit will be cut every year; national debt will fall and the current budget return to surplus as soon as possible, independently verified by the OBR. The core belief: Britain only succeeds when working families succeed—through fair rewards for work, strong public services, and power devolved to communities.

Economic foundations and fair taxes
- Restore fiscal credibility while tackling the causes of the deficit through higher productivity and rising living standards.
- Fairer taxes: restore the 50p top rate; introduce a 10p starting rate funded by ending the Marriage Allowance; abolish non-dom status; no rises in basic or higher Income Tax, NI or VAT; tough action on avoidance.
- Back small business: cut and then freeze business rates for 1.5m small firms; create a British Investment Bank and regional banks; boost competition in banking; levy payday lenders to support credit unions.
- Long-term growth: National Infrastructure Commission; HS2 with cost control and better northern rail; strategic roads and cycling; swift airport decision; universal affordable high-speed broadband and better mobile coverage.
- Lead the low-carbon transition: legal 2030 decarbonised power target; empower the Green Investment Bank; Energy Security Board; one million new green jobs.

Better work, pay and chances for young people
- Raise the National Minimum Wage to £8+ by Oct 2019; promote the Living Wage via procurement and Make Work Pay contracts; require listed firms to report Living Wage status.
- Ban exploitative zero-hours contracts and close the agency worker loophole; scrap employment tribunal fees.
- Rebalance corporate governance to favour long-termism, curb excessive pay, and give employees a voice.
- Create a gold-standard technical route: Technical Baccalaureate and Technical Degrees; guarantee an apprenticeship for every school leaver with the grades; cut tuition fees to £6,000; end unpaid internships lock-out. Fund a Compulsory Jobs Guarantee via a bank bonus tax.

Cutting the cost of living and fixing broken markets
- Freeze energy bills until 2017 and reform the market with a tough new watchdog; drive energy efficiency.
- Water affordability scheme and stronger regulation.
- Rail reform with a public operator option; fare freeze then strict caps; powers for city/region-wide integrated transport.
- Build at least 200,000 homes a year by 2020; first call for local first-time buyers; new garden cities; tackle land banking.
- Fair renting: three-year tenancies the norm, cap excessive rent rises, ban letting fees. Abolish the Bedroom Tax.
- Family support: free childcare rising from 15 to 25 hours for working parents of 3–4-year-olds; guarantee wraparound care 8am–6pm; double paternity leave to four weeks and increase pay.

World-class NHS and care, and high-quality education
- Rescue the NHS: 20,000 more nurses, 8,000 more GPs, 3,000 more midwives funded by a Mansion Tax, a tobacco levy and anti-avoidance; 48-hour GP appointments; one-week cancer tests.
- Repeal the Health and Social Care Act; NHS preferred provider; cap private profits; integrate physical, mental and social care; parity for mental health; focus on prevention.
- End 15-minute care visits; recruit 5,000 home-care workers; support carers.
- Protect the entire education budget; all teachers qualified; cap infant class sizes at 30; new School Standards Directors; boost vocational excellence.

Safe, cohesive communities with fair immigration
- Protect neighbourhood policing (safeguard over 10,000 officers); a Victims’ Law; tougher action on domestic abuse and child exploitation; ban legal highs.
- Counter extremism with community-led Prevent, stronger oversight, and proportionate powers.
- Controlled, fair immigration: 1,000 extra border staff, full exit checks, two-year wait for benefits, English requirement for public-facing roles; ban wage undercutting and rogue agencies.

Power closer to people and rights protected
- English Devolution Act: £30bn and major powers to city and county regions; local Public Accounts Committees; Constitutional Convention; replace the Lords with a Senate of the Nations and Regions; votes at 16.
- Clean politics: tougher lobbyist register; ban MPs’ paid directorships; extend FOI; media plurality and full Leveson implementation; protect the Human Rights Act; require large firms to publish gender pay gaps; race equality strategy. Keep Channel 4 public; free museum entry; give fans a voice in football clubs.

Britain in the world
- Reform the EU from within; lock any future power transfers behind a referendum; uphold NATO; defence review; maintain a minimum credible nuclear deterrent; strengthen cyber security.
- Lead on climate change towards global net zero in the second half of the century.
- Keep 0.7% aid, focus on the poorest, support universal health coverage.

A fully funded, credible plan to rebuild a fairer, more secure Britain—together.
